candidates.attacker_control: Attacker controls (a) the mediapackage XML posted as the `mediaPackage` form parameter of `POST /ingest/ingest` or `POST /ingest/ingest/{workflowDefinitionId}` (IngestRestService.ingest, lines 1178–1213) — element `<track uri=...>` is parsed by MediaPackageParser/MediaPackageImpl with no URI validation (only MediaPackageSupport.sanityCheck on the identifier, lines 324–328 of MediaPackageSupport.java), and (b) the workflow definition id, selectable among role-visible definitions (WorkflowDefinitionScanner.userCanAccessWorkflowDefinition returns true when a definition has no roles, as is the case for studio-upload/fast/schedule-and-upload in etc/workflows). Reachability requires an account with ROLE_ADMIN, ROLE_CAPTURE_AGENT or ROLE_STUDIO for `/ingest/**` (etc/security/mh_default_org.xml:350-352); no admin role is needed for starting the workflow on the submitted mediapackage (WorkflowServiceImpl.start only requires a non-null, known user, lines 490–533). The content written is fetched from an attacker-chosen URI (external HTTP server or the cluster's own WFR/distribution URL).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked and ruled out as mitigations: (1) MediaPackageSupport.sanityCheck only validates a non-blank identifier, not element URIs (lines 324-328). (2) toSafeName sanitizes only the last path segment (no `..`, slash or leading dot) — it does not sanitize the directory part built from the URI (WorkingFileRepositoryImpl 119, 236-247). (3) StaticResourceServlet blocks `..` in path (lines 181-185) and WorkingFileRepositoryImpl.put/getFile/putInCollection call checkPathSafe (lines 350-353, 518-521, 655-657), showing the intended defense exists elsewhere but is missing in toWorkspaceFile/getElementDirectory/moveTo. (4) `ingest-download` deletes the just-downloaded URI afterwards (`workspace.delete(originalUri)`, IngestDownloadServiceImpl 283-289), which can remove the dropped file in that particular workflow; workflows whose first media operation is `inspect` (e.g. studio-upload/fast) leave the file in place. (5) Anonymous/users without ROLE_CAPTURE_AGENT/ROLE_STUDIO cannot reach /ingest/** (etc/security/mh_default_org.xml:350-352); the issue is privilege escalation/persistence from an authenticated low-privilege account, not unauthenticated access. (6) JAX-RS UriBuilder.fromUri is not expected to normalize dot segments (no normalize() call in toWorkspaceFile), and PathSupport.concat performs no normalization (PathSupport.java 53-71); I could not run code to confirm this, so it is stated as an assumption.
candidates.impact: Authenticated but low-privileged users (capture agents / Studio users) can make the server write attacker-controlled content to an arbitrary path writable by the Opencast service user, outside the workspace/WFR root (directory chosen by the attacker, filename limited by toSafeName to characters matching [\w.-]). This can overwrite or plant files used for persistence or code execution depending on deployment (e.g. `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, user service units, config/working files), or corrupt/deny service data. The related unguarded read helpers can cause arbitrary local files to be returned/parsed as mediapackage content. No runtime exploitation was performed; this is a source-level trace.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) Authenticated capture-agent/Studio (or admin) account able to call /ingest/**. 2) Pick a workflow definition that resolves the element URI to a local file — e.g. `inspect` (present in default `studio-upload`/`fast`, runs on every track: InspectWorkflowOperationHandler lines 160–183) or `ingest-download` (included in `schedule-and-upload`/`partial-ingest`). 3) For a write, the attacker serves the payload at an HTTP URL whose path contains enough `../` segments to escape the workspace root (e.g. http://attacker.example/x/../../../../../../home/opencast/.ssh/authorized_keys); the final filename passes toSafeName() (WorkingFileRepositoryImpl lines 119, 236–247) as long as it has no slash, `..` or leading dot (e.g. `authorized_keys`, `config.json`).
candidates.root_cause: WorkspaceImpl.toWorkspaceFile(URI) builds the destination path by concatenating the workspace root with the directory part of a caller-supplied URI (serverPath = FilenameUtils.getPath(uri) via UriBuilder; PathSupport.concat(wsRoot, serverPath)) and never normalizes the result or verifies that it stays under wsRoot. Only the final filename goes through toSafeName(); the directory portion keeps `../` segments. The resulting File is used for mkdirs(), touch(), FileOutputStream (downloadTo) and move operations. MediaPackage element URIs are accepted verbatim from HTTP-submitted mediapackage XML, and workflow operations (inspect, ingest-download, encode/compose, moveTo, etc.) pass them to Workspace.get()/read(). The same pattern exists in the related path helpers: WorkingFileRepositoryImpl.getElementDirectory() (used by moveTo/copyTo without checkPathSafe), DistributionPathUtils.getLocalFile() and AssetPathUtils.getLocalFile() (prefix check + Paths.get without normalization).
candidates.title: Path traversal in workspace URI-to-file mapping allows arbitrary file write (and read) outside the workspace via /ingest
candidates.trace: POST /ingest/ingest[/{wdID}] → IngestRestService.ingest (1178-1213, parses attacker mediapackage, starts workflow) → IngestServiceImpl.ingest (1230-1291) → WorkflowServiceImpl.start (490-533, no ACL/write check) → workflow operation `inspect` (InspectWorkflowOperationHandler 160-183) or `ingest-download` (IngestDownloadServiceImpl 249-289) → media inspect/enrich → MediaInspector.inspectTrack (94-107, workspace.get(trackURI)) → WorkspaceImpl.get (359-402) → WorkspaceImpl.toWorkspaceFile (813-833: serverPath = FilenameUtils.getPath(uriString); PathSupport.concat(wsRoot, serverPath); wsDirectory.mkdirs(); new File(wsDirectory, toSafeName(name))) → WorkspaceImpl.downloadIfNecessary (514-547) → downloadTo (567-576: dst.createNewFile(); new FileOutputStream(dst); copyLarge) — writes attacker content to the traversed path. The same URI→path mapping is used by WorkspaceImpl.read (405-438, which can resolve attacker URIs to arbitrary local files through DistributionPathUtils.getLocalFile 110-129 / AssetPathUtils.getLocalFile 114-152) and by WorkspaceImpl.moveTo (750-773) / WorkingFileRepositoryImpl.moveTo-copyTo via getElementDirectory (741-777, 580-582), where `checkPathSafe` (497-502) is applied in put/getFile but not in these helpers.
candidates.unverified: Static analysis only; no code was executed and no exploit payload was sent. The exact runtime behavior of jakarta/javax.ws.rs UriBuilder.fromUri(...).replaceQuery(null).build().toString() with `..` segments, the concrete default filesystem locations (wsRoot, workspace/service user home), and whether a specific deployment's workflow definitions/config make an `inspect`-style operation run before any delete are deployment-dependent. I did not find an existing containment/normalization patch anywhere else in this tree, but I cannot diff against upstream to confirm the exact fix commit.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 (and CWE-73): Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory — path traversal / external control of file path

coverage_summary: Source tree: 2731 files (2731 visible to me; binary-like files are skipped by the reader). Per the index scope, 1738 Java files were parsed and 2624 files indexed, with 107 source files missing from the index, no semantic resolution and no data-flow/control-flow analysis. I focused on Java backend code: REST/JAX-RS endpoints and their servlet/security mappings (etc/security/mh_default_org.xml), the ingest → workflow → workspace/working-file-repository path, authorization logic (XACML/AccessControlUtil/Series/Search/Workflow/SecurityUtil/UserDirectory), XML parsing helpers, URL signing, GraphQL, transcription callbacks, and shared filesystem utilities. I did not review every one of the ~1700 Java files (e.g. much of scheduler, OAI-PMH, Elasticsearch index internals, LTI/OAuth filters, most workflow operations, front-end JS/CSS/JSON assets and documentation) and I did not execute any code, tests or scanners.
limitations: Read-only review without executing code, tests, builds or exploit payloads; no runtime confirmation of any finding.
The source-relation index is syntactic/navigation-only: no data-flow, control-flow, semantic resolution or reachability proof; its 'facts' are name-based hints, and 107 files are absent from it.

The snapshot is a large multi-module OSGi project; I could not exhaustively inspect all Java files, so other issues may exist that I did not see (I explicitly did not deep-dive scheduler, OAI-PMH, Elasticsearch internals, LTI/OAuth security filters, most WOHs, and most front-end assets).

The exploitability of the submitted candidate depends on deployment-specific configuration (workspace root and permissions, which workflow operations run, the concrete role assignment of ROLE_STUDIO/capture-agent accounts) that cannot be verified from source alone.
I could not diff against upstream or inspect any fix/commit history, so I cannot say whether this specific defect corresponds to a previously published advisory.

rejected_leads.lead: Unauthenticated IBM Watson transcription callback (POST /transcripts/watson/results is ROLE_ANONYMOUS in etc/security/mh_default_org.xml:369-370; IBMWatsonTranscriptionRestService.reportStatus uses the body's user_token/id without a shared secret or job/event ownership check)
rejected_leads.reason: Only reachable when the IBM Watson transcription service is enabled/configured, requires knowledge/existence of a transcription job id, and the service updates job state/saves result files rather than exposing data; impact and reachability are weaker than the chosen candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: GraphQL /graphql is ROLE_ANONYMOUS and only UserQueryExtension.searchUser carries @RolesAllowed; event/series queries and mutations rely entirely on lower-layer ACL checks (GraphQLServlet, EventMutationExtension, DeleteEventCommand, UpdateEventAclCommand)
rejected_leads.reason: The GraphQL bundle is an opt-in tech preview (opencast-plugin-graphql = off by default in etc/org.opencastproject.plugin.impl.PluginManagerImpl.cfg), and the underlying IndexService/SeriesService/AssetManager paths do perform ACL-based checks, so I could not substantiate a concrete bypass with source evidence.

rejected_leads.lead: External API includeInternalPublication parameter exposes internal publication URLs to any ROLE_API_EVENTS_PUBLICATIONS_VIEW user (EventsEndpoint.getPublications, lines 1700-1705) with no admin check
rejected_leads.reason: Looks like the intended API feature (version-gated, documented parameter) rather than a missing check; no evidence that internal channel URLs contain secrets or grant access by themselves.

Real inconsistency, but in the moveTo flow getFile() still calls checkPathSafe on the same ids and aborts before the file move (IllegalArgumentException), so I could not show a clean arbitrary write through that helper alone; it is reported as part of the same root-cause family as the chosen candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Search REST leading-wildcard full-text queries (SearchRestService wildcardQuery("fulltext", "*"+q+"*")) as a possible search DoS
rejected_leads.reason: Changelog and code show the 16.7 fix for CVE-2024-52797 is already applied (bounded limits, 250-result cap for non-admins), and I did not find a remaining measurable DoS.

summary: Repository is Opencast 17.x (pom 17-SNAPSHOT, changelog through 17.5, June 2025), a large Java/OSGi media-processing platform. I reviewed REST endpoints (ingest, search, external-api, admin-ui, graphql, playlists, annotation, WFR/static files), core authorization code (XACMLAuthorizationService, AccessControlUtil, SeriesServiceDatabase, WorkflowServiceImpl, SecurityUtil, UserDirectoryUtils), security configuration (etc/security/mh_default_org.xml), XML parsing (XmlSafeParser), and file/URI handling (WorkspaceImpl, WorkingFileRepositoryImpl, AssetPathUtils/DistributionPathUtils). Most security controls looked correct (XXE centrally mitigated, SQL parameterized, deny-wins ACLs, role checks in search/index endpoints). The strongest issue I could substantiate from source is a missing path-containment check when a mediapackage element URI is translated into a workspace file path: attacker-supplied `..` segments survive into the filesystem path, so workflow operations that call `workspace.get()/read()` on an element URI can read or write files outside the workspace. I chose that single candidate.
